content.title: IF YOU EAT {{THIS}} EVERY DAY... THIS IS WHAT HAPPENS
facts: If you ate **beets** every day for 2 weeks, your blood pressure would likely drop as the nitrates widen your blood vessels, and workouts would suddenly feel easier.
If you ate **oats** every day for 30 days, your cholesterol numbers would start to shift as the beta-glucan fiber grabs onto bile acids and pulls them out of your body.
If you ate **sardines** every day for 3 weeks, your joints would feel less stiff as the omega-3s calm down low-grade inflammation around them.
If you ate **kimchi** every day for 2 weeks, your digestion would feel noticeably smoother as the live cultures repopulate your gut with helpful bacteria.
If you ate **Brazil nuts** every day for 1 week, your energy and mood could lift slightly, thanks to a big dose of selenium supporting your thyroid.
If you ate **blueberries** every day for 1 month, your memory and focus could sharpen as plant compounds called anthocyanins protect brain cells from wear and tear.
If you ate **lentils** every day for 2 weeks, your blood sugar swings would smooth out, since the fiber and protein combo slows how fast glucose hits your bloodstream.
If you ate **walnuts** every day for 3 weeks, your skin could look calmer and less inflamed, helped along by their plant-based omega-3s.
**Follow along** – for more daily health tips like this.

caption:
Beets get a bad reputation for staining everything purple, but inside your body that same pigment is doing real work — the nitrates convert into nitric oxide, which relaxes and widens blood vessels so blood (and oxygen) moves more freely. Oats work differently: the beta-glucan fiber forms a gel in your gut that traps bile acids made from cholesterol, forcing your liver to pull more cholesterol out of your blood to make new bile. And sardines bring EPA and DHA straight into your joints and bloodstream, where they get converted into compounds that actively dial down inflammation instead of just avoiding foods that cause it. Everyone's body responds a little differently, so pay attention to how yours reacts.
